bat-removal.intro: Ward is a small Saluda County town in the ridge country between Saluda and Johnston — a handful of streets of older homes in pine-and-farm country, where the housing stock is pre-war and postwar, the attics are tall and quiet, and big brown bats have held some of them for as long as the houses have stood. The creeks running to the Saluda River feed the evening insect hatch the colonies hunt, and the town's stillness does the rest: a Ward attic above a house whose owners are away at work all day, or away for a season, is a maternity roost of the first quality, and the colonies found here are usually found late — by staining, by smell, by a stray in the hall.
bat-removal.extendedBody:
Late discoveries in the ridge country

Ward's bat work runs to established colonies, so the method is the thorough one: map every exit by its staining and flight line before anything is sealed, fit one-way devices at the active entries when the season allows, and close every secondary gap on the roofline in the same programme. South Carolina fixes no bat dates by law; SCDNR's guidance — never seal while pups are flightless — is the working rule, and a colony mapped in June is excluded when the young are flying, at a price quoted once. The guano question in a long-held attic is answered with photographs and a measurement, not a sales pitch, and quoted separately if removal is warranted. In ridge-country towns the same houses are prospected by bat scouts every spring; a completely sealed roofline is the only answer that holds for more than a season, and it is the version we quote.

faqs.q: How much does bat removal cost in Ward?
faqs.a: It depends on the colony's size and the number of entries — the older homes here tend to present several, across gables, eaves, and chimney flashing. We inspect and map first, then quote the complete exclusion firmly, with attic cleanup quoted separately only if the inspection shows it is needed. If the colony is found while pups are flightless, the mapping happens at the first visit and the exclusion is scheduled for its window at the same quoted price.

faqs.q: Our Ward home is empty for part of the year. Would bats move in while we are away?
faqs.a: They are the most likely tenant a quiet house gets. Bat scouts prospect rooflines every spring, and an undisturbed attic with an open gable screen or a fascia gap is claimed quickly — by the time owners return, a maternity colony can be established with young. The prevention is a seal done while you are in residence: every gap closed in metal and screen, documented with photographs so you can verify it from away. It is far cheaper than the exclusion-plus-cleanup that an occupied season produces, and in a small town it is the version of the job that only has to be done once.
